patches.why: ⭐ A THIRD OUTCOME — THE DEFECT IS MIGNE'S, THE WORD WAS OURS. The plate prints *mutiles* (PL 114 p. 323, col. 0635D, VERS. 23, read 2026-08-29 from the on-disk scan, corner numbers checked first): 'Non omnes questiones vitandae, sed mutiles et sine disciplina.' *mutiles* is itself defective — Migne has dropped the initial i of *inutiles* — so the [sic:] SHOULD fire here. But Corpus Corporum misread his m as an n, so our English was accusing him of *nutiles*, a form he never set. The Latin is corrected to what the plate prints and THE MARKER STANDS with its quotation fixed to [sic: *mutiles*]. ⚑ This is the case the sweep would have missed if it had only asked 'is the marker true or false': a marker can be right about the page and wrong about the word.
